chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: 'When you combine between the two salats, do not perform optional (prayers) between the two.'

key_terms.الصلاتين: The two prayers/salats; in fiqh context refers to the paired prayers combined together (Dhuhr-Asr or Maghrib-Isha')
key_terms.تطوع: Voluntary/supererogatory prayer (nafl); prayers performed in addition to the five obligatory salats
key_terms.جمعت: To combine/gather; the act of performing two obligatory prayers in succession during one time period

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform nafl prayers between combined obligatory prayers in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), likely Imam al-Kazim, issued a ruling that when a believer combines two obligatory prayers (such as Dhuhr and Asr, or Maghrib and Isha'), no voluntary or optional (nafl/tatawwu') prayers should be performed between them. This ruling reflects the jurisprudential principle that combining prayers is a concession granted for certain circumstances, and inserting voluntary prayers between the two would effectively separate them, thereby nullifying the combining.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Al Husayn Bin Sayf, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I heard himasws saying: ‘When you gather between the two Salāts, so do not perform Optional Salāts between the two’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from al-Husayn ibn Sayf from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Muhammad ibn Hakim who has said the following: “I once heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘
If you perform two Salah (prayer), one after the other, do not perform optional Salah (prayer) between them.”’
